learning: Next iteration: if the robot holds the line with few line-loss events, raise base_speed toward 1.5 and kp slightly; if steering_oscillation is high, lower kp or raise kd; if line_loss_events are high on the slalom, test wider outer weights or a different line_loss direction. Check whether the outer sensors ever read non-zero (the 2 cm pitch may leave a gap).
notes: Baseline runnable package: Builder geometry unchanged, controller tuned from contract physics. Gains are conservative (kp 2.0, ki 0, kd 0.05, base_speed 1.2) so the first race shows stability before speed is raised.
rationale: Iteration 0 has no race telemetry, so the controller is built from the contract physics and the Builder's stated intent, not from measured tuning. Geometry is kept exactly as proposed so the first race tests the baseline. The sensors sit at x = -0.04 (right) to +0.04 (left), so the outer sensors take weights -2 and +2, the middle ones -1, 0 and +1, which makes the signal sign match the contract (positive = steer left, and a line on the left side reads positive). Because the 12 mm footprints sit on a 2 cm pitch, a centred line covers mainly the middle sensor, so the signal is small near centre and grows as the line drifts outward. kp = 2.0 gives a full-scale turn of about ±4 (about ±1400 PWM) at the array edge, which is enough correction without saturating. kd = 0.05 adds mild damping against overshoot. ki = 0 avoids integral wind-up on the bends. base_speed = 1.2 is a moderate start (60 percent PWM demand) so the first race reveals whether the 0.7 kg, 0.12 m platform can hold the line before speed is pushed toward 1.5 m/s. line_loss = 'last_direction' keeps the robot turning toward the side it last saw the tape, which suits bends better than a fixed search direction. I expect completion on the oval and s-bend; the slalom is the most likely to produce line-loss events.
